draw.description: Drawing commands in order: rect, circle or path, each with a color.

checked.description: true, false, or empty (null) for a box that is neither: a parent of some checked children.

label.description: Text beside it that is part of what you press, and what a screen reader calls it.

value.description: 0 to 1; leave out, or give nothing, for a wait with no end.

track.description: The colour role of the track behind the indicator.

label.description: What a screen reader calls it.

disabled.description: Dimmed, not focusable, and its handlers do not run.

measured_width.description: Output: how wide it is laid out. Bind a Signal or a state name to read it (written after layout and when the window resizes).

measured_height.description: Output: how tall it is laid out.

closed.description: The names of the closable panels that are shut; a close button adds its panel, and taking a name out opens the panel again.

title.description: The panel's tab, when its zone has several.

closable.description: Its tab has a close button.

path.description: SVG path data to draw instead of a named icon.

view_box.description: [min_x, min_y, width, height] the path is drawn in; Material Symbols' 0 -960 960 960 when not given.

src.description: A path relative to the file.

fit.description: How the picture fills its box.

alt.description: What the picture shows, for a screen reader. Without it the picture is decorative and hidden from one.

frame.description: A video frame, (rgba, width, height), pushed from a ViewModel.

value.description: 0 to 1; leave out, or give nothing, for a wait with no end.

track.description: The colour role of the track behind the indicator.

buffer.description: 0 to 1: how much has loaded, drawn as a lighter bar behind the value.

stop_indicator.description: A dot at the end of the track (Material 3).

label.description: What a screen reader calls it.

text.description: The link's text, which names it for a screen reader.

typography_role.description: A type role of the theme, such as body_large or title_large.

wrap.description: 'word' breaks a long line; 'none' never does.

max_lines.description: The most lines shown, from 1; a longer text is cut (with `overflow: ellipsis`, an ellipsis ends the last line).

letter_spacing.description: Extra space between letters, in pixels (tracking).

href.description: A web or mail link (http, https, mailto, tel) opened in the OS's browser or mail program when it is activated.

visited.description: Whether it has been followed; opening its href sets it, and a rule can show it with `state: visited`.

underline.description: When the text is underlined: while the pointer is over it or it has the keyboard focus, always, or never.

label.description: What a screen reader calls it.

edges.description: The links: each {from: id, to: id}, the ids of the GraphNodes.

snap.description: A node the user moves lands on a multiple of this many pixels; 0 is no grid.

arrows.description: Each edge ends in an arrowhead.

fit.description: Pan and zoom, when it opens, so every node shows (never beyond actual size).

open.description: Whether it is showing. Closing it (Escape, a press outside) writes false back to a Signal it is bound to.

anchor.description: The name of a node in this view to sit against, or `parent` for the node it is written inside; without one it is centred in the window.

placement.description: Which side of the anchor; it flips or shifts to fit.

modal.description: Dims the window behind it, blocks input to it, and keeps focus inside.

dismissible.description: Escape and a press outside close it.

focus_first.description: When it opens, the focus moves to the first thing in it that can take it (a menu's first row).

timeout.description: Closes itself this many milliseconds after it opens, unless the pointer is over it; 0 never.

group.description: Buttons with one group are exclusive.

label.description: Text beside it that is part of what you press, and what a screen reader calls it.

disabled.description: Dimmed, not focusable, and its handlers do not run.

orientation.description: Which way it scrolls. Horizontal lays its children out in a row and `scroll_direction` is 'right' or 'left'.

snap.description: When scrolling stops it settles on the nearest child that has a `snap_align` style, with that edge of the child at the same edge of the view.

scroll_offset.description: The scrolled distance; scrolling writes it back to a Signal it is bound to.

at_top.description: Output: whether it is scrolled to the start. Bind a Signal or a state name to read it.

at_end.description: Output: whether it is scrolled as far as it goes.

scroll_direction.description: Output: 'down' or 'up' (a horizontal one: 'right' or 'left') for the last scroll, 'none' before the first.

value.description: From `min` to `max`; a bound Signal follows the drag.

step.description: Snap to multiples of this from `min`; the keys move by it.

ticks.description: A mark at each step (needs `step`): a discrete slider.

value_indicator.description: A bubble with the value over the handle while it is dragged or has the keyboard.

vertical.description: Stood up: the bottom is `min`; `style.height` is its length and `style.width` the touch target's.

size.description: MD3 Expressive's size: a thicker track in two pieces and a thin 4 px handle (empty: the standard 4 px track and 20 px handle).

icon.description: An icon inset at the start of the track (needs a `size` of `s` or larger).

label.description: What a screen reader calls it.
What a screen reader calls it.

decimals.description: How many decimal places show (empty: only as many as the number needs).

prefix.description: Shown before the number, such as a currency sign.

suffix.description: Shown after the number, such as a unit.

wrap.description: A step past one bound lands on the other (needs min and max).

orientation.description: horizontal puts the panes side by side, vertical one above the other.

position.description: How much of the room the first pane has, from 0 to 1. Dragging the handle writes it back to a Signal it is bound to.

min_first.description: The least the first pane can be, in pixels.

min_second.description: The least the second pane can be, in pixels.

collapsible.description: A double click on the handle closes the first pane, and opens it again.

label.description: What a screen reader calls the handle.

src.description: A .svg or .svgz file, relative to the view.

content.description: The SVG text, instead of a file.

alt.description: What the picture shows, for a screen reader. Without it the picture is decorative and hidden from one.

label.description: Text beside it that is part of what you press, and what a screen reader calls it.

icons.description: A check on the handle when on and a cross when off.

typography_role.description: A type role of the theme, such as body_large or title_large.

wrap.description: 'word' breaks a long line; 'none' never does.

max_lines.description: The most lines shown, from 1; a longer text is cut (with `overflow: ellipsis`, an ellipsis ends the last line).

letter_spacing.description: Extra space between letters, in pixels (tracking).

selectable.description: The text can be selected and copied.

heading.description: Makes it a heading of this level for a screen reader.

placeholder.description: Shown, dimmed, while the field is empty.

multiline.description: Several lines; Enter makes a new one.

obscured.description: Shows dots instead of the text, and blocks copy and cut (a password).

max_length.description: The most characters it takes; 0 is no limit.

read_only.description: The text can be selected and copied but not changed.

mask.description: A pattern the typed text is put in: # a digit, A a letter, * either, \ a literal; other characters come by themselves.

hour.description: 0 to 23; a press keeps the half of the day it is in.

minute.description: 0 to 59, in fives on the face.

mode.description: Which hand the face shows and sets; letting go in hour mode moves on to minutes.

auto_advance.description: Letting go in hour mode moves on to the minutes.

label.description: What a screen reader calls it.

item_height.description: How tall every row is, in pixels.

overscan.description: Rows built beyond each edge of what is in view.

scroll_offset.description: The scrolled distance; scrolling writes it back to a Signal it is bound to.

at_top.description: Output: whether it is scrolled to the start.

at_end.description: Output: whether it is scrolled as far as it goes.

scroll_direction.description: Output: 'down' or 'up' for the last scroll, 'none' before the first.

remember.description: true, or a name: the window's size, place (where the platform lets an app say) and maximized state are kept between runs.

fullscreen.description: The window fills its monitor, borderless (set when the view loads).

transparent.description: A see-through window that draws only what the view paints; the OS fixes it before the window opens.

blur_behind.description: The desktop behind a transparent window is blurred (where the compositor does it).

click_through.description: Clicks go to the window beneath; the window takes none.

title_bar.description: Title, icon and buttons of a custom title bar.
